item.title: Early pAncharAtrika state
item.description:
For pAncharAtra/ vaiShNava origin in yajur-veda/ Adhvaryava movement, see - TW.

Oldest pAncharAtrika is nArAyaNIya in MBh, which has the 4 vyUha-s with association with jIva-s etc.. Classical claim was always - pAncharAtra was closely affiliated with yajur-veda (ekAyana shAkhA).

‘Pancharatra is also veda only, the shandilya statement is not literal but figurative’ was the mainstream position of early pancharatrikas, and they didn’t see themselves as transgressive, and there’s nothing too unique about Ramanuja’s defence.

item.title: EkAyana gAyatrI
item.description:
Source: TW

Chief reason was that they did not chant the usual Savitri mantra(Gayatri) that is recited during sandhyavandana by usual Brahmins. Instead they chanted Narayana ashtakshari, Vāsudeva dvādashākshari and Vishnu Gayatri in the three sandhyas or only Vishnu Gayatri in all the three sandhyas.

item.title: Mukta bodha intro
item.description:
Roots

Contained within the Mahābhārata, the Nārāyaṇīya teaches that the divine reality is comprised of a processual formation (vyūha) that, taken as a whole, is Viṣṇu-Nārāyaṇa himself. Each facet of the divine person (Nārāyaṇa, Vāsudeva, Saṃkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, and Aniruddha) corresponds to a succession of states within each human being (thinking, feeling, willing, knowing, acting) and also to the process whereby a person loses track of, and then recovers, an awareness of their true nature.

item.title: अध्य्-एकायनम्
item.description:
अभिप्रायान्तरम्

एकायनशाखा कठस्यैवोपशाखासीद् इत्यनिमेषः - द्वयोर् अपि काश्मीरमूलत्वात्।
मानसतरङ्गिणीकृतो ऽभिप्रायः पृथग् रक्षितः।

Source: RavilochanaH

There is no record of an ekayana shakha in sukla yajur Veda. Rather pAncharAtra texts talk abt kanva shakha only. Otoh a pancaratra sruti and pancaratra upanishad are quoted by kashmira shaiva acharyas like utpala. My presumption is that just as taittiriya shakha has vaikhanasa branch with its own mantrapatha, pancaratrins must have been of kanva shakha with some mantrapatha/sruti of their own.

item.title: आगमाडम्बरे पाञ्चरात्रिकाः
item.description:
विस्तारः (द्रष्टुं नोद्यम्)

I’ve searched through both volume’s of Witzel’s Veda in Kashmir and extant material seems to confirm the ritvik’s assertion that no one outside the Pancharatrika-s themselves considered them to have any unique/worthwhile Vedic material (not counting Sarvagamapramanya followers) - Andra

OFFICIANT. That these Pāñcarātrika Bhāgavatas adopt Brahmanical manners.²
They mix with brahmins and have no scruples about using the form of greeting that only we may use to our equals. They recite the Pāñcarātra scriptures with a special pattern of accented syllables, as if they were taking the text of Veda as their example.³ ‘We are brahmins’: this is how they speak of themselves, and ….
